 The US president, Donald Trump , has arrived in Manila, the capital of the Philippines, for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit, where he is due to meet south east Asian leaders and take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.
 After departing from the Boeing 747 gifted to him by Qatar, Trump was greeted by officials and members of the military on the red carpet laid out on the Ninoy Aquino International Airport’s tarmac.
 The US president, weakened by the midterm results , is arriving at the Asean summit on the day it concludes, and is reportedly not due to make any significant policy or diplomatic announcements.

 9m ago 05.16 EST China slams new US chip curbs and pledges 'necessary measures'
 Graeme Wearden China has threatened to retaliate against the US after Washington tightened restrictions on remote access to AI chips and servers. 
 At a press conference on Tuesday, China’s foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing would take “necessary measures” to safeguard its own interests, saying:
 double quotation mark The US has repeatedly overstretched the concept of national security, abused export controls and even interfered in China’s normal trade and technological cooperation with other countries, unjustifiably suppressing the development of China’s hi-tech industries.” 
 Guo also called the US move a typical example of economic coercion that deviates from the consensus reached by both countries, Reuters reports .
 As we blogged yesterday , the US Commerce Department has issued a new rule which limits remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips by companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil.
 The new measure closes a loophole which allowed Chinese companies to access cutting-edge American technologies by using datacentres based in other countries in Asia.
 Awkwardly for Beijing, the new “interim final rule” is being imposed just as Donald Trump prepares to meet China’s president Xi Jinping on Thursday in Shenzhen, which is hosting this week’s Apec summit .
 China vows to take ‘necessary measures’ against US AI chip restrictions, as investors brace for Nvidia’s results – business live Read more Share 23m ago 05.03 EST Trump was also greeted by Philippine children waving US flags as a rendition of ‘YMCA’ was played by a military band. He is now being flown to the Solaire hotel where he is due to spend most of his brief visit to Manila.
 The meeting with America’s “Quad” security allies, Japan, Australia and India, an expected US-Thailand trade deal signing and a dinner will all be held where the president is staying.

Photograph: Eloisa Lopez/EPA Share Updated at  05.12 EST 47m ago 04.38 EST Trump arrives in Manila for first leg of high-profile trip to Asia
 The US president, Donald Trump , has arrived in Manila, the capital of the Philippines, for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit, where he is due to meet south east Asian leaders and take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.
 After departing from the Boeing 747 gifted to him by Qatar, Trump was greeted by officials and members of the military on the red carpet laid out on the Ninoy Aquino International Airport’s tarmac.
 The US president, weakened by the midterm results , is arriving at the Asean summit on the day it concludes, and is reportedly not due to make any significant policy or diplomatic announcements.
 Share Updated at  05.06 EST 54m ago 04.32 EST Apec: what to watch for and key sticking points
 Middle East instability: The economic ripple effects of the US-Israel war on Iran, such as risks to energy security, trade flows, supply chains and inflation are major concerns.
 Tripartite dynamics: All eyes are on the scheduled Trump, Xi and Putin meeting on Thursday. China is hesitant to engage in talks on nuclear disarmament, as it has fewer such weapons than the other two, analysts said. It is unclear to what extent, if at all, the Iran war and Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine will be discussed.
 China-US relations : Both sides are falling short on ​commitments to an extended trade truce. Rare ​earth supplies, AI and tariffs are also likely ​to figure on the agenda. US arms sales to Taiwan will also be closely watched.
 China’s ties with Japan and the Philippines: Strains ​in Japan and China ties have ‌persisted since Japan’s prime minister Sanae Takaichi angered ​Beijing in November 2025 by ​suggesting that Japan could deploy its military if a Chinese move against Taiwan also threatened its territory. China-Philippines relations will likewise be closely watched amid continuing tension in the disputed South China Sea.
 Share 1h ago 04.10 EST During a ​meeting with Xi Jinping , Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum said ⁠that her country wanted to strengthen ​cooperation with ‌China in ‌areas related ‌to technology, agriculture, water resources, health and tourism.
 The two leaders were speaking in the southern ​Chinese tech and manufacturing hub of ⁠Shenzhen , which is hosting the Apec summit . An annual summit of CEOs is taking place today and tomorrow; while the Apec economic leaders’ meeting is set for tomorrow and Thursday.
 View image in fullscreen Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum (L) speaks as her foreign minister Roberto Velasco Alvarez (R) looks on during a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/EPA Share Updated at  04.52 EST 2h ago 03.32 EST As we mentioned in a previous post , hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against the arrival of Donald Trump in Manila (expected in an hour or so), with many protesters angry at the new US-led Pax Silica initiative on AI and critical minerals.
 The Guardian Australia’s political editor, Tom McIlroy , explains why so many people are rejecting the initiative and provides some details about what it entails: 
 Pax Silica has sparked tensions in the Philippines over plans to build a tech hub outside Manila that critics say will affect water and energy supplies, and displace members of the Ayta Indigenous community.
 Pax Silica will include a technology hub planned at New Clark City in Tarlac, about 120km from Manila.
 Intended to bolster western stocks of AI technology and reduce “excessive dependencies” on single source supply chains, including from China, Pax Silica will provide chips and critical minerals to 25 participating signatory governments.
 View image in fullscreen Indigenous people from the Cordillera region hold a protest at Bonifacio Park in Manila, condemning Trump's upcoming visit to the Philippines for the Asean summit. Photograph: Charles Edmon S Perez/JNA/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock Share 3h ago 02.54 EST The Philippines president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr , has called for concrete safeguards for food and energy supplies across south east Asia and east Asia in order to protect households and businesses from higher prices caused by global supply disruptions.
 He said the impact of conflicts (such as the US-Israel war on Iran) has caused prices and energy costs to rise across the region, hitting consumers hard.
 “A disruption thousands of miles away can reach households across east and southeast Asia through the price of rice, the cost of energy, or the loss of a day’s income,” Marcos Jr was quoted as having said. The Philippines president said it is imperative to keep maritime trade and logistics moving and secure essential supplies to withstand shocks.
 “Our task today is to put our collective strength to work. In ships reaching their destinations, in reliable supplies of food and energy, in businesses continuing to operate, and in families facing the future with greater confidence,” he said.
 View image in fullscreen Ferdinand Marcos Jr (C) speaks on the sidelines of the Asean Summit on 17 November 2026 in Manila, the Philippines. Photograph: Jam Sta Rosa/Pool/Getty Images Share Updated at  03.02 EST 3h ago 02.16 EST China is hosting the summit for the third time, after Shanghai (2001) and Beijing (2014). Both domestic ​and international reasons govern the choice of Shenzhen, said Chim Lee, ‌senior analyst at the Economist Intelligence Unit.
 As part of China’s Greater Bay Area home to Hong Kong and Macau, which Beijing seeks to establish ‌as a global hub for technology and innovation, the city offers a platform to showcase China’s vision for development and trade.
 It also highlights Shenzhen’s resilience to geopolitical turbulence, Lee added. Shenzhen is the base for several Chinese auto and tech companies, such as BYD, Huawei and Tencent.
 View image in fullscreen A delivery man rides past a sign promoting Apec in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China. Photograph: Ng Han Guan/AP Share 3h ago 02.08 EST France and Malaysia agree series of deals, including rare earths
 France and Malaysia upgraded bilateral ⁠ties to a strategic ⁠partnership and ​announced a slew of cooperation deals today , with Kuala Lumpur agreeing to relax export curbs on raw rare earths to support joint development in ⁠the sector.
 The announcement came following a meeting between French president Emmanuel Macron and Malaysia’s prime minister Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur. Macron is on a two-day visit ​to Malaysia, his first since 2017.
 View image in fullscreen Emmanuel Macron attends a meeting with Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Photograph: Fazry Ismail/POOL EPA/AP “This renewed partnership will contribute to strengthen our independence on both sides,” ‌Macron said, adding it would also boost the two countries’ defence and security.
 Anwar said Malaysia has agreed to export some raw rare earths materials to France following a commitment by Paris to collaborate on rare earths processing.
 Share 3h ago 02.01 EST Interim summary
 It has just gone 3pm in Manila (host to the Asean summit) and Shenzhen (Apec). Here’s the main news from both cities so far today. There is plenty more to come so stay with us.
 China will ⁠cut $280m in tariffs on Canadian ​exports including pork and seafood , Mark Carney’s office said after he met with Xi Jinping. Carney hailed “greater predictability and stability” in China-Canada relations.
 Canada and ​China also agreed to extend by two years ⁠existing remission measures for certain ​Chinese ​steel and ​aluminium products .
 Papua ⁠New Guinea’s prime minister James Marape ⁠confirmed that Taiwan does not operate in ⁠the Pacific country anymore , during a meeting ⁠with Xi ​in Shenzhen. “We hope this assists you in your efforts for reunification,” Marape added.
 Donald Trump is flying on the new Air Force One, gifted to him by Qatar, to Manila where a meeting with Quad leaders is scheduled for later today.
 Japan ⁠has proposed creating a task force to coordinate cooperation in Asia on oil stockpiling and the release of supplies during emergencies – ⁠one that will allow ⁠neighbours ​in the region to use idle storage capacity in Japan.
